title: Not a C-beauty user? You might soon be, as Chinese brands make global push - South China Morning Post
text:
A K-beauty rival? C-beauty brands take on the global market with lines in Ulta, Boots | South China Morning Post Fashion & Beauty - Fashion & Beauty Not a C-beauty user? You might soon be, as Chinese brands make global push Advertisement Beauty Lifestyle Fashion & Beauty A K-beauty rival? C-beauty brands take on the global market with lines in Ulta, Boots 
 If your make-up and skincare routines do not already include C-beauty, they soon could as brands like Proya and Florasis expand globally
 3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN Listen Reuters Published: 12:45pm, 7 Nov 2026 China’s beauty brands are stepping into the global market, armed with intricately carved lipsticks, ⁠freeze-dried face masks activated with purified water, and creams infused with traditional Chinese medicine ingredients.
 Proya Cosmetics, the largest C-beauty brand by revenue, is among the most aggressive. Its Advanced Firming and Original Repair skincare lines will be sold in 400 Ulta stores and on Ulta.com across the United States from this month, and it opened a Paris research and development centre in October.
 Other brands began with online sales and are now expanding to physical stores abroad. They include Florasis, whose lipsticks and other ornate cosmetics draw on traditional Chinese aesthetics. It opened its first overseas flagship shop in Tokyo’s Ginza district last year.
